newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Monday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing
prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover fell to 1.9 billion yuan from 2.9 billion yuan last Friday with the 60-day contract again the most active.
Traders said the fall in turnover was mainly the result of financial institutions, especially state banks, trading less with the approach of the Chinese lunar new year holiday.
The 60-day contract was again the most active one because it straddles the Chinese new year holiday, before which the demand for funds is certain to increase, said a local trader.
Traders said the rates were unlikely to move down due to the gradually increasing demand for funds and the receding expectation of an early cut in bank interest rates.

"The higher-than-expected return for the new two-year treasury note, the first treasury note of 1997, indicates that the interest rates will not be cut in the short term," said a second trader. "It will support rates in the next few days."
